cross_stage_scored.s1: Age-related decline in ABCA1- and ABCG1-mediated free-cholesterol efflux traps cholesterol in RPE lysosomes, impairing photoreceptor outer-segment digestion and accelerating GA; enhancing efflux or inhibiting SOAT1 is predicted protective.
cross_stage_scored.s2: Age-related decline in ABCA1/ABCG1 efflux combined with SOAT1-driven cholesteryl esterification traps free cholesterol in RPE lysosomes, and pharmacologic SOAT1 inhibition liberates this lipid load for residual transporter-mediated efflux, restoring photoreceptor outer-segment digestion.

cross_stage_scored.s1: Age-related decline in ABCA1- and ABCG1-mediated free-cholesterol efflux traps cholesterol in RPE lysosomes, impairing photoreceptor outer-segment digestion and accelerating GA; enhancing efflux or inhibiting SOAT1 is predicted protective.
cross_stage_scored.s2: Inhibit SOAT1 catalytic activity with an ocularly delivered small molecule (K-604/nevanimibe class), optionally paired with LXR-mediated upregulation of ABCA1/ABCG1, to restore net cholesterol efflux from RPE lysosomes.

cross_stage_scored.s1: Age-related decline in ABCA1- and ABCG1-mediated free-cholesterol efflux traps cholesterol in RPE lysosomes, impairing photoreceptor outer-segment digestion and accelerating GA; enhancing efflux or inhibiting SOAT1 is predicted protective.
cross_stage_scored.s2: Drusen and GA are characterized by unesterified cholesterol and cholesteryl ester deposition in the RPE and Bruch's membrane, and cholesterol-trafficking loci (ABCA1, APOE, LIPC, CETP) are established AMD risk genes.

cross_stage_scored.s1: Age-related decline in ABCA1- and ABCG1-mediated free-cholesterol efflux traps cholesterol in RPE lysosomes, impairing photoreceptor outer-segment digestion and accelerating GA; enhancing efflux or inhibiting SOAT1 is predicted protective.

cross_stage_scored.s2: Excess RPE65-driven visual-cycle flux generates all-trans-retinaldehyde faster than ABCA4, RDH8, RDH10, and ALDH1A1 can clear it, leading to cytotoxic A2E bisretinoid accumulation that impairs RPE lysosomal function and drives RPE cell death in geographic atrophy.

cross_stage_scored.s2: Cross-species genetics and functional characterization (PMID 42685076) implicate CNN2 as an AMD susceptibility gene, and its actin-binding role sits at a proximal node governing focal adhesion survival signaling, daily phagocytic clearance of photoreceptor outer segments, and basal matrix turnover — the three processes whose failure drives drusen accumulation and RPE monolayer collapse in geographic atrophy.

cross_stage_scored.s1: AMD-risk CNN2 variants reduce calponin-2/MYH9-dependent actomyosin traction in subretinal ITGAM+ macrophages, slowing their migration and phagocytic clearance of drusen material and thereby prolonging complement-activating debris deposition.
cross_stage_scored.s2: Unlike single-downstream-effector approaches, restoring CNN2 addresses cytoskeletal collapse upstream of all three pathways simultaneously.

cross_stage_scored.s1: AMD-risk CNN2 variants reduce calponin-2/MYH9-dependent actomyosin traction in subretinal ITGAM+ macrophages, slowing their migration and phagocytic clearance of drusen material and thereby prolonging complement-activating debris deposition.
cross_stage_scored.s2: In vitro: human iPSC-derived RPE with CRISPRi or siRNA CNN2 knockdown (or patient-risk-variant lines), with readouts of fluorescent photoreceptor outer segment phagocytosis, phalloidin F-actin organization, p-PTK2 and p-RPS6 Western blot (mTOR activity), transepithelial electrical resistance, and basolateral MMP14 activity in Transwell cultures, comparing AAV-CNN2 rescue versus vehicle.

cross_stage_scored.s2: In vivo: RPE-specific Cnn2 knockout mice (Best1-Cre or AAV8-Best1-Cre crossed lines) with readouts of fundus autofluorescence-defined atrophy area, SD-OCT outer retinal thickness, scotopic ERG amplitudes, and basal laminar deposit burden at 12 months, with subretinal AAV rescue as the efficacy endpoint.

cross_stage_scored.s1: Loss-of-function variants in complement regulators CFI and CFH together with gain-of-function C3/CFB alleles drive assembly of an intracellular C3 convertase (complosome) in RPE cells, causing autologous C3b deposition and sublytic C5b-9 (MAC) injury that kills RPE cells and enlarges geographic atrophy lesions.
cross_stage_scored.s2: Silencing CFB in the eye collapses the alternative-pathway amplification convertase (C3bBb) that runs unrestrained when CFH regulation is lost, simultaneously shutting down C3b/iC3b opsonization, C5b-9 (MAC)-driven RPE lysis, and C5a generation for C5AR1-dependent CCR2+ monocyte recruitment.

cross_stage_scored.s1: Loss-of-function variants in complement regulators CFI and CFH together with gain-of-function C3/CFB alleles drive assembly of an intracellular C3 convertase (complosome) in RPE cells, causing autologous C3b deposition and sublytic C5b-9 (MAC) injury that kills RPE cells and enlarges geographic atrophy lesions.
cross_stage_scored.s2: Inhibit (knock down) CFB locally via intravitreally delivered siRNA/ASO, with optional low-dose hepatic CFB knockdown, to restore complement homeostasis despite CFH loss-of-function and CFB gain-of-function.

cross_stage_scored.s1: Loss-of-function variants in complement regulators CFI and CFH together with gain-of-function C3/CFB alleles drive assembly of an intracellular C3 convertase (complosome) in RPE cells, causing autologous C3b deposition and sublytic C5b-9 (MAC) injury that kills RPE cells and enlarges geographic atrophy lesions.
cross_stage_scored.s2: Factor B is the obligate catalytic subunit of the alternative-pathway C3 and C5 convertases, so CFB inhibition acts upstream of every effector arm in the hypothesis (opsonization, MAC lysis, C5a-C5AR1 chemotaxis) with a single intervention.

cross_stage_scored.s2: Genetic proof-of-concept exists: reducing Cfb in Cfh-/- mice corrects the retinal C3 deposition caused by factor H deficiency, directly modeling the human CFH-LOF architecture of GA risk.

cross_stage_scored.s2: Because C3/C5 inhibitors already slow GA progression clinically but are limited by injection burden and ocular inflammation, an intravitreal CFB-silencing approach offers a longer-acting, upstream mechanistic match to the top-ranked hypothesis.

cross_stage_scored.s2: Age-related HPSE activity cleaves sulfated heparan sulfate chains from HSPG2 (perlecan) and syndecan proteoglycans in Bruch's membrane, removing the glycosaminoglycan docking sites for CFH and permitting uncontrolled alternative-pathway complement deposition on RPE and choriocapillaris in geographic atrophy.

cross_stage_scored.s1: Loss-of-function variants in complement regulators CFI and CFH together with gain-of-function C3/CFB alleles drive assembly of an intracellular C3 convertase (complosome) in RPE cells, causing autologous C3b deposition and sublytic C5b-9 (MAC) injury that kills RPE cells and enlarges geographic atrophy lesions.
cross_stage_scored.s2: Inhibit HPSE enzymatic activity in the outer retina/Bruch's membrane (e.g., intravitreal or topical delivery of an HS-mimetic heparanase inhibitor such as pixatimod/PG545 or a small-molecule HPSE inhibitor) in order to preserve sulfated HS chains, restore CFH anchoring, and re-establish local alternative-pathway complement regulation without systemic complement suppression.

cross_stage_scored.s1: Loss-of-function variants in complement regulators CFI and CFH together with gain-of-function C3/CFB alleles drive assembly of an intracellular C3 convertase (complosome) in RPE cells, causing autologous C3b deposition and sublytic C5b-9 (MAC) injury that kills RPE cells and enlarges geographic atrophy lesions.
cross_stage_scored.s2: GA lesion growth is clinically validated as complement-driven (pegcetacoplan and avacinacaptad pegol slow atrophy), yet intravitreal C3/C5 blockade carries infection and neovascularization risks, motivating restoration of endogenous local regulation instead.

cross_stage_scored.s2: Bruch's membrane HS proteoglycans are known binding sites for CFH via its glycosaminoglycan-interacting domains, and heparanase expression and HS fragmentation increase with age and oxidative stress in the outer retina.

cross_stage_scored.s2: Blocking HPSE would therefore keep CFH positioned at the RPE/choroid interface, suppressing C3 convertase activity and MAC deposition at the site of atrophy rather than pan-complement inhibition.

cross_stage_scored.s2: In vitro, culture primary human fetal or iPSC-derived RPE on perlecan-rich matrix, treat with recombinant HPSE, and quantify CFH binding (ELISA/western blot), HS stub generation (3G10 immunostain), and alternative-pathway activation (Bb, C3b, C5b-9 deposition) with and without pixatimod rescue.

cross_stage_scored.s2: In vivo, use aged C57BL/6J or Ccl2-/-/Cx3cr1-/- GA-model mice with intravitreal HPSE inhibitor versus vehicle, reading out HPSE activity and HS stubs in Bruch's membrane, CFH/MAC immunolocalization by confocal microscopy, quantitative OCT and fundus autofluorescence for atrophy area, and ERG for retinal function, with endpoint comparison at 3 and 6 months.

cross_stage_scored.s2: Complement risk genotypes (CFI/CFH loss-of-function plus C3/CFB gain-of-function) enable assembly of an intracellular alternative-pathway C3 convertase in RPE cells, causing autologous C3b deposition and sublytic C5b-9 injury that drives RPE cell death and geographic atrophy enlargement.

cross_stage_scored.s2: Inhibit C3/CFB convertase assembly inside RPE using a cell-penetrant compstatin-class C3 inhibitor (or intracellular CFB inhibitor) delivered to the RPE, optionally combined with restoration of CFI cofactor activity via RPE-targeted expression or recombinant factor I.

cross_stage_scored.s1: Loss-of-function variants in complement regulators CFI and CFH together with gain-of-function C3/CFB alleles drive assembly of an intracellular C3 convertase (complosome) in RPE cells, causing autologous C3b deposition and sublytic C5b-9 (MAC) injury that kills RPE cells and enlarges geographic atrophy lesions.
cross_stage_scored.s2: Genetic evidence consistently places alternative-pathway dysregulation at the center of GA risk, and failure of CFI/CFH-mediated C3b inactivation would permit runaway intracellular convertase activity (complosome) specifically in the stressed RPE.

cross_stage_scored.s1: Loss-of-function variants in complement regulators CFI and CFH together with gain-of-function C3/CFB alleles drive assembly of an intracellular C3 convertase (complosome) in RPE cells, causing autologous C3b deposition and sublytic C5b-9 (MAC) injury that kills RPE cells and enlarges geographic atrophy lesions.

cross_stage_scored.s2: In vivo, test the compound in Cfh-deficient or CFI-haploinsufficient mice with sodium iodate or aging-induced RPE injury, quantifying RPE/Bruch's membrane C3 deposition by immunohistochemistry and atrophy lesion area by fundus autofluorescence and OCT.

cross_stage_scored.s1: Age-related decline of DICER1 ribonuclease activity in RPE permits accumulation of cytotoxic Alu retroelement RNA, which activates the p38-MAPK-MAPKAPK5 (MK2) stress kinase axis to induce RPE degeneration independently of inflammasome signaling.
cross_stage_scored.s2: Age-related loss of DICER1 in RPE allows Alu RNA accumulation that drives RPE death through p38alpha-MAPK (MAPK14) and its downstream kinase MAPKAPK5/MK2, and this cytotoxic arm can be severed pharmacologically without engaging complement or inflammasome pathways.

cross_stage_scored.s1: Age-related decline of DICER1 ribonuclease activity in RPE permits accumulation of cytotoxic Alu retroelement RNA, which activates the p38-MAPK-MAPKAPK5 (MK2) stress kinase axis to induce RPE degeneration independently of inflammasome signaling.
cross_stage_scored.s2: Inhibit the kinase activity of p38alpha (MAPK14) and its effectors MAPKAPK2/MAPKAPK5 in RPE using a locally delivered (intravitreal) small-molecule p38 inhibitor, thereby decoupling accumulated Alu retroelement RNA from RPE degeneration; an AAV-mediated DICER1 re-expression adjunct could address the upstream enzymatic deficit.

cross_stage_scored.s1: Age-related decline of DICER1 ribonuclease activity in RPE permits accumulation of cytotoxic Alu retroelement RNA, which activates the p38-MAPK-MAPKAPK5 (MK2) stress kinase axis to induce RPE degeneration independently of inflammasome signaling.
cross_stage_scored.s2: DICER1 levels decline in the aging human RPE and Alu RNA is elevated in GA lesions, and Alu RNA alone induces RPE degeneration in mice via a p38-MAPK-dependent, inflammasome-independent cell death program (Kaneko et al., Nature 2011).

cross_stage_scored.s1: Age-related decline of DICER1 ribonuclease activity in RPE permits accumulation of cytotoxic Alu retroelement RNA, which activates the p38-MAPK-MAPKAPK5 (MK2) stress kinase axis to induce RPE degeneration independently of inflammasome signaling.
cross_stage_scored.s2: Because atrophy enlargement in GA is driven substantially by cell-autonomous RPE death, blocking the terminal kinase effector arm should slow lesion growth even if upstream Alu accumulation or DICER1 loss is not corrected.

cross_stage_scored.s1: Age-related decline of DICER1 ribonuclease activity in RPE permits accumulation of cytotoxic Alu retroelement RNA, which activates the p38-MAPK-MAPKAPK5 (MK2) stress kinase axis to induce RPE degeneration independently of inflammasome signaling.
cross_stage_scored.s2: Use two complementary models: (1) human iPSC-derived RPE monolayers transfected with in vitro-transcribed Alu RNA, treated with p38 inhibitors (e.g., BIRB 796, losmapimod) versus vehicle, with readouts of p-p38/p-HSP27 (MAPK14/MAPKAPK2 phosphorylation) by immunoblot, TUNEL/caspase-3 cleavage, and transepithelial resistance; (2) C57BL/6J mice given subretinal or intravitreal Alu RNA, or RPE-specific Dicer1 conditional knockout mice, dosed intravitreally with p38 inhibitor, with RPE flatmount TUNEL/ZO-1 staining, fundus autofluorescence, and OCT-based atrophy area as primary readouts.

cross_stage_scored.s1: Age-related failure of PINK1-PRKN-mediated mitophagy, worsened by loss of DRD2-dependent mitophagy support and only incompletely compensated by BNIP3L upregulation, retains depolarized ROS-producing mitochondria and leaks mtDNA into the RPE cytosol, driving mitochondrial-to-nuclear stress signaling, NLRP3 activation and RPE cell death.
cross_stage_scored.s2: Activate DRD2 (with a repurposable systemic or topical D2 agonist, e.g., bromocriptine/quinagolide-type) to pharmacologically restore PINK1-PRKN mitophagy flux and secondarily suppress downstream NLRP3 inflammasome activation in RPE.

cross_stage_scored.s1: Age-related failure of PINK1-PRKN-mediated mitophagy, worsened by loss of DRD2-dependent mitophagy support and only incompletely compensated by BNIP3L upregulation, retains depolarized ROS-producing mitochondria and leaks mtDNA into the RPE cytosol, driving mitochondrial-to-nuclear stress signaling, NLRP3 activation and RPE cell death.
cross_stage_scored.s2: In GA, RPE cells accumulate depolarized, ROS-producing mitochondria because PINK1-PRKN mitophagy fails; retained organelles leak mtDNA into the cytosol, engaging NLRP3 and inflammatory cell death that expands atrophy.

cross_stage_scored.s1: Age-related failure of PINK1-PRKN-mediated mitophagy, worsened by loss of DRD2-dependent mitophagy support and only incompletely compensated by BNIP3L upregulation, retains depolarized ROS-producing mitochondria and leaks mtDNA into the RPE cytosol, driving mitochondrial-to-nuclear stress signaling, NLRP3 activation and RPE cell death.
cross_stage_scored.s2: Recent evidence of age-related retinal monoamine dysregulation in AMD-like retinopathy supports dopaminergic mitophagy support as the druggable node, since BNIP3L compensation is insufficient.

cross_stage_scored.s2: Test in hiPSC-RPE from GA donors (or ARPE-19) transduced with mt-Keima, challenged with CCCP or rotenone/antimycin A, with or without DRD2 agonist; readouts include mitophagy flux by mt-Keima flow cytometry, cytosolic mtDNA by ddPCR for MT-CYB, and NLRP3 output by caspase-1 cleavage and IL-1beta release.

cross_stage_scored.s2: Inhibit the NACHT-domain ATPase activity and oligomerization of NLRP3 with a selective small-molecule inhibitor (MCC950/dapansutrile-class) delivered intravitreally to arrest inflammasome assembly in RPE.

cross_stage_scored.s2: Load human iPSC-derived RPE or primary hfRPE monolayers with A2E, irradiate at 430 nm and pulse with amyloid-beta oligomers to model drusen-borne dual signal, then treat with an NLRP3 inhibitor; readouts include ASC speck formation and caspase-1 activity (FLICA/imaging), IL1B release by ELISA, GSDMD-N terminus cleavage by immunoblot, and monolayer integrity by TEER and LDH release.

cross_stage_scored.s1: Cytosolic DNA from leaky mitochondria or reverse-transcribed retroelements activates the CGAS-STING1-TBK1-IRF3 axis in RPE, producing chronic type I interferon (IFNB1) and CXCL10 that recruit CXCR3+ cytotoxic CD8 T cells and NK cells to form a cytotoxic front enlarging the atrophic lesion.
cross_stage_scored.s2: Chronic activation of the MB21D1(cGAS)–STING1–TBK1–IRF3 axis in stressed RPE sustains IFNB1/CXCL10 output that recruits CXCR3+ CD8 T and NK cells, which form the cytotoxic front enlarging the atrophic lesion.

cross_stage_scored.s2: Locally (intravitreal or topical) inhibit STING1 with a small-molecule antagonist (palmitoylation-site inhibitor class, e.g., H-151 analogs), with MB21D1 enzymatic inhibitors as a backup arm, to extinguish the downstream type I IFN–CXCL10 gradient without systemic immunosuppression.

cross_stage_scored.s2: Confirm in vivo in A2E-photostressed or ABCA4-/- mice by measuring RPE/outer-retinal atrophy area on fundus autofluorescence and OCT with corresponding reduction in caspase-1 and cleaved GSDMD staining on RPE flat mounts.

cross_stage_scored.s1: NCOA4-mediated ferritinophagy elevates labile ferrous iron while GPX4 inactivation and ACSL4-dependent incorporation of oxidizable PUFAs into membranes (despite SLC7A11 import) unleash lipid peroxidation that executes ferroptotic RPE death and expands GA.

cross_stage_scored.s1: Downregulation of ADARB1 (ADAR2) abolishes Q/R-site editing of GRIA2, generating calcium-permeable AMPA receptors that elevate dendritic calcium influx and CAPN1/caspase cascade activation, driving motor neuron excitotoxic degeneration.
cross_stage_scored.s2: Loss of ADARB1-mediated A-to-I editing at the GRIA2 Q/R site produces arginine-to-glutamine substitution in unedited AMPA receptors, rendering them calcium-permeable and triggering dendritic calcium overload, CAPN1 and caspase cascade activation, and motor neuron excitotoxic death.

cross_stage_scored.s2: Restore or potentiate ADARB1 expression and catalytic activity (or deploy a site-directed RNA-editing strategy) to re-establish near-complete Q/R-site editing of GRIA2 transcripts, thereby eliminating calcium-permeable AMPA receptors and blunting downstream calpain/caspase activation.

t2_reversal_scored.s1: C02 rests on the strongest causal evidence in GA biology—CFH risk haplotypes and protective CFB alleles converge on alternative-pathway C3 convertase control, and complement-driven C3b/C5b-9 deposition on RPE is directly implicated in lesion growth, whereas C03 GSDMD-pyroptosis mechanism is plausible but rests on weaker, mostly indirect human evidence.
t2_reversal_scored.s2: C02 edges out on causal anchoring, since CFH risk and protective CFB alleles converging on convertase control represent the strongest human-genetic evidence in GA, whereas C03 inflammasome-to-GSDMD axis is well supported histopathologically (NLRP3/CASP1 at the atrophy margin) but the dominance of pyroptotic lysis in RPE dropout is less proven; C03 nonetheless earns credit for targeting the terminal executor with cell-type-restricted logic and thoughtful preservation of IL-18 homeostatic outputs.

t2_reversal_scored.s1: C01 integrates Bruch's membrane aging (HS 6-O/2-O desulfation), extracellular matrix biochemistry, and the strongest GA genetics (CFH risk haplotypes, including variants known to impair glycosaminoglycan binding) into a multi-layer mechanistic account of local alternative-pathway dysregulation at the correct anatomic interface; C07 is a linear, largely established pathway whose specific TLR3-caspase signaling is partly contested and whose causal support, while strong, is already known.
t2_reversal_scored.s2: C07 rests on a causally validated, cell-autonomous chain—DICER1 loss and Alu RNA are each sufficient to induce RPE degeneration in mice and DICER1 is reduced in human GA tissue—giving it strong mechanistic depth, whereas C01 SULF2-HSPG2-CFH link is plausible and well anchored in complement biology but more inferential, lacking direct in vivo causal support in GA.

t2_reversal_scored.s1: C06 presents a deeper, multi-node mechanistic chain (SLC7A11 cystine import, GPX4 inactivation, ACSL4-PUFA substrates, TFRC iron influx) anchored in an RPE-specific vulnerability—the constitutive PUFA-peroxide load from daily outer-segment phagocytosis—and coherently addresses both initiating and executing defects; C10 is elegant and complement-relevant but narrower, resting on a single glycation-stripping event at CD59.
t2_reversal_scored.s2: Both proposals offer coherent, multistep causal chains with RPE-specific grounding; C10 links a defined metabolic lesion (dicarbonyl stress) to the exact terminal effector implicated in GA pathogenesis (CD59 loss unleashing C5b-9), while C06 assembles a thorough ferroptosis cascade anchored in the RPE's daily phagocytic PUFA burden, so this is a tie.

t2_reversal_scored.s1: C09 presents a deeper, multi-layered causal chain (HFE genetics -> HAMP upregulation -> SLC40A1 degradation -> labile iron expansion -> Fenton-driven DNA damage -> senescence/atrophy) with a genetic risk anchor (HFE polymorphisms) and a falsifiable distinction between the Fenton-DNA arm and ferroptosis lipid markers; C10 is disease-relevant given terminal complement centrality in GA but its cascade is more linear and rests on a narrower CD59-glycation premise.
t2_reversal_scored.s2: C10 causal chain (dicarbonyl stripping of GPI-anchored CD59 → unopposed C9 polymerization/sublytic C5b-9 → Ca2+ influx/NFKB1/apoptosis) is internally consistent, anchored in well-established terminal-complement pathology of GA, and coherently explains why broad proximal complement blockade has underperformed; C09 is plausible and supported by Perls'-staining and HFE genetic data, but its mapping of HFE risk alleles onto hepcidin-driven SLC40A1 internalization in RPE is internally awkward, since HFE loss typically lowers rather than raises hepcidin, and it conflates systemic and inflammatory-local HAMP regulation.

t2_reversal_scored.s1: C09 constructs a multi-layer causal chain (HFE risk variants → HAMP upregulation → SLC40A1 internalization → labile iron expansion → Fenton-mediated DNA damage) that is anchored by histologically documented RPE iron in GA and HFE genetic risk data, and it explicitly contrasts its Fenton-DNA arm against ferroptosis-lipid readouts, adding falsifiable specificity; C10 rests on the well-validated terminal-complement injury axis but is more linear and borrows heavily from the diabetic glycated-CD59 literature.
t2_reversal_scored.s2: C10 is anchored in the dominant complement-driven pathophysiology of GA with a precise molecular checkpoint (dicarbonyl-mediated stripping of GPI-anchored CD59), yielding a tight causal chain from glycoxidative stress to sublytic C5b-9 injury, calcium influx, NFKB1 activation, and apoptosis; C09 is plausible and genetically supported (HFE, documented RPE iron overload) but its longer inferential chain (complement -> HAMP -> SLC40A1 loss -> labile iron -> Fenton DNA damage) is less directly coupled to the primary disease lesion.

t2_reversal_scored.s1: Both proposals are mechanistically coherent, but C06 causal chain is more tightly tailored to RPE-specific biology — the constitutive PUFA-lipid peroxide burden from daily outer-segment phagocytosis makes the cystine/GSH/GPX4 dependence argument uniquely compelling for GA, and it addresses both the initiating (SLC7A11 loss) and executing (GPX4 inactivation) defects in one transcriptional program; C08 cGAS-STING-senescence loop is plausible and well-articulated but leans on a more indirect path from interferon signaling to RPE dropout.
t2_reversal_scored.s2: C08 posits a specific, stepwise cell-autonomous loop (oxidized mtDNA -> cGAS -> STING -> TBK1/IRF3 -> IFNB1/STAT1 -> senescence/SASP/dropout) that maps cleanly onto established GA biology of RPE senescence and inflammatory dropout, with every node experimentally verifiable; C06 ferroptosis narrative is coherent but rests on a less-established premise that chronic oxidative stress suppresses SLC7A11/GPX4 in RPE (NRF2-target genes are usually stress-induced), making its initiating-defect claim comparatively generic.

t2_reversal_scored.s1: C01 wins by integrating the strongest GA evidence base (alternative complement activation, CFH haploinsufficiency/Y402H as top genetic risk) with a concrete extracellular aging mechanism (SULF2-mediated 6-O-desulfation of perlecan HS erasing CFH docking sites), explaining how aging can phenocopy genetic CFH dysfunction locally; C04 is coherent and grounded (DICER1 loss, Alu accumulation) but leans on a less clinically validated type I IFN axis and must compete with the originally implicated NLRP3/MyD88 pathway downstream of Alu RNA.
t2_reversal_scored.s2: C04 rests on a well-documented causal chain (DICER1 loss, cytosolic Alu RNA/DNA, cGAS-STING-driven interferon signaling and RPE degeneration) with published in vivo sufficiency data, whereas C01 perlecan desulfation-SULF2-CFH link is coherent and grounded in known CFH-heparan sulfate biology but the specific causal role of SULF2 in Bruch's membrane aging and GA remains largely hypothetical.

t2_reversal_scored.s1: C03 presents a tight, linear causal chain (drusen/bisretinoid lysosomal rupture to NLRP3-CASP1-GSDMD) anchored at the atrophy margin, and its executor-level blockade preserves upstream homeostatic outputs like IL18, a mechanistically elegant distinction; C06 multi-node ferroptosis argument is coherent but rests on a partially circular oxidative-stress premise (oxidative load both suppresses SLC7A11 and inactivates GPX4) and is less resolved mechanistically.
t2_reversal_scored.s2: C06 is deeper and better anchored in RPE-specific physiology, tying constitutive phagocytosis of PUFA-rich outer segments, documented retinal iron accumulation, and GPX4/SLC7A11 essentiality into a coherent initiating-plus-executing death pathway, whereas C03 inflammasome-centric narrative, while coherent and cell-type-restricted, rests on a more contested literature in which NLRP3 roles in AMD models have proven double-edged.

t2_reversal_scored.s1: C02 is anchored by the strongest causal evidence in AMD biology—convergent CFH risk and CFB protective haplotypes at the same convertase node, plus clinical validation of the pathway by approved C3/C5 inhibitors—whereas C07 DICER1-Alu/TLR3 axis is coherent and supported by human tissue and mouse sufficiency data but rests on a narrower, partly contested evidence base.
t2_reversal_scored.s2: Both proposals are mechanistically coherent and disease-relevant; C07 rests on direct causal evidence (DICER1 depletion and Alu RNA each suffice to induce RPE degeneration, with a defined TLR3-CASP8-CASP3 execution pathway), while C02 rests on strong convergent human genetics (CFH risk and protective CFB alleles at the convertase-control node) plus complement deposition in GA eyes, so this is a tie between cell-autonomous causality and population-genetic causality.

t2_reversal_scored.s1: C06 chain from SLC7A11 loss and GPX4 inactivation through ACSL4/TFRC-amplified lipid peroxidation to ferroptotic RPE death is tightly anchored in established GA pathophysiology (daily PUFA-rich outer segment phagocytosis, retinal iron accumulation, 4-HNE/MDA adducts) and directly explains the atrophy endpoint, whereas C08 oxidized mtDNA-cGAS-STING-IFNB1-STAT1-senescence cascade is plausible but more indirect about how RPE cells actually die and how senescence drives lesion expansion.
t2_reversal_scored.s2: C08 provides a tightly coupled, cell-autonomous causal chain (oxidized mtDNA -> cGAS/STING -> TBK1/IRF3 -> IFNB1/STAT1 -> senescence/SASP/RPE dropout) with a specific self-ligand rationale and a clear explanation for chronicity, whereas C06 ferroptosis narrative, while coherent, is a more generic oxidative-stress-to-cell-death extension.

t2_reversal_scored.s1: C03 targets the terminal executor of RPE death at the atrophy margin, making it mechanistically proximal to the lesion-generating event while preserving upstream inflammasome outputs; C05 addresses an upstream degradative bottleneck, but A2E/bisretinoids are largely undegradable even with restored lysosomal machinery, and C05 premise of selectively disinhibiting only the MTORC1-TFEB axis while sparing other MTORC1 outputs is mechanistically questionable.
t2_reversal_scored.s2: C05 causal chain (MTORC1-phosphorylated TFEB sequestration suppressing CLEAR-network lysosomal genes, driving lipofuscin/A2E accumulation) rests on well-established biochemistry with in vivo support from RPE mTORC1-hyperactivation models and directly targets the widely accepted lysosomal-insufficiency basis of GA, whereas C03 premise that GSDMD-dependent pyroptosis dominates RPE dropout at the atrophy border competes with ferroptosis and complement-mediated death as the implicated modes, and its claim that GSDMD blockade preserves IL18 output is shaky since GSDMD pores themselves mediate IL18 secretion.

t2_reversal_scored.s1: C05 ties the central, well-documented GA lesion (lipofuscin/A2E accumulation from lysosomal insufficiency) to a validated master-regulator bottleneck (MTORC1-phosphorylated TFEB), and its systems-level rescue logic is mechanistically deeper than C06 ferroptosis narrative, whose causal primacy in GA lesion expansion remains less established relative to complement-driven cell death.
t2_reversal_scored.s2: C06 offers a more direct mechanistic chain to the defining endpoint of geographic atrophy—RPE cell death and lesion expansion—by tying the RPE-specific PUFA phagocytic burden to SLC7A11/GPX4 failure and iron-driven lipid peroxide execution, whereas C05 addresses an upstream accumulation phenotype (lipofuscin/A2E) whose causal link to RPE death is more debatable and whose premise of constitutive MTORC1 hyperactivity in GA RPE is less firmly established.

t2_reversal_scored.s1: C08 presents a coherent, linear causal chain (oxidized mtDNA -> cGAS -> STING/TBK1-IRF3 -> IFNB1/STAT1 -> senescence and SASP-driven RPE dropout) that maps directly onto established GA pathology and recent literature on cytosolic mtDNA sensing in stressed RPE. C09 mechanism is plausible and grounded in documented RPE iron accumulation and HFE risk associations, but contains internal tensions: HFE variants classically reduce rather than enhance HAMP signaling, and simultaneously 'unloading ferritin' via efflux while 'augmenting FTH1 buffering' pulls in opposite directions, weakening mechanistic coherence.
t2_reversal_scored.s2: C09 integrates human histopathology (documented RPE iron in GA), a genetic risk modifier (HFE), and a chemically precise damage arm (Fenton-derived hydroxyl radicals → mtDNA/nuclear DNA lesions) with a built-in strategy to dissociate the DNA-damage arm from ferroptosis lipid peroxidation; its main weakness is the murky directionality of HFE polymorphisms versus local HAMP upregulation. C08 cGAS-STING-IFNB1-senescence cascade is coherent and grounded in RPE oxidative-stress biology, but it is a more generic signaling narrative whose IFNB1-centric causality in RPE dropout remains less directly evidenced.

t2_reversal_scored.s1: C01 unifies the strongest GA evidence—CFH/Y402H risk genetics, alternative-pathway C3/C5b-9 deposition, and age-related heparan sulfate loss in Bruch's membrane—into one causal chain in which SULF2 desulfation phenocopies the impaired GAG docking of the risk variant, whereas C04 DICER1/Alu premise is human-validated but its extension to a cGAS-STING-IFNB1-dominant axis in RPE is more inferential and type I interferon-driven pathology is less established in GA than complement or inflammasome biology.
t2_reversal_scored.s2: C04 rests on directly documented GA pathology (DICER1 decline, cytosolic Alu accumulation, causal RPE degeneration in models) with a coherent, well-mapped signal transduction cascade to IFN-driven death, whereas C01 chain from age-related HS desulfation to CFH loss is plausible and elegantly ties to CFH genetics, but attribution of desulfation specifically to SULF2 (versus reduced biosynthetic sulfation) is a weaker evidentiary link.

t2_reversal_scored.s1: C03 is anchored in well-documented NLRP3 inflammasome activation and pyroptosis-marker enrichment at the GA margin, and its executor-level logic (blocking GSDMD lysis while preserving non-lytic IL18 outputs) is mechanistically sound; C07 DICER1/Alu-TLR3-CASP8 axis has strong causal mouse data but rests on contested human DICER1-loss findings and is entangled with DICER1's miRNA functions, making its human disease relevance less secure.
t2_reversal_scored.s2: C07 rests on a rigorously established causal chain—DICER1 reduction in GA human tissue, sufficiency of both DICER1 knockdown and subretinal Alu RNA to induce RPE degeneration in vivo, and defined TLR3-CASP8-CASP3 signaling—making it an upstream, cell-autonomous etiologic mechanism, whereas C03 GSDMD-mediated pyroptosis at the atrophy margin is plausibly supported but rests on correlative inflammasome markers and models (Abca4/Rdh8, Ccl2/Cx3cr1) that imperfectly recapitulate RPE dropout.

t2_reversal_scored.s1: C05 wins on mechanistic depth and disease specificity — it names a precisely characterized biochemical node (MTORC1-mediated S142/S211 phosphorylation of TFEB) whose inhibition directly explains the hallmark lipofuscin/bisretinoid accumulation that precedes geographic atrophy, and its 'master regulator' rationale coherently restores an entire degradative program rather than one arm. C06 is mechanistically rich but leans on the less-established claim that ferroptosis is the dominant executioner of RPE loss in GA, repackaging the classic oxidative-stress hypothesis in ferroptosis vocabulary.
t2_reversal_scored.s2: C06 causal chain terminates directly in the defining pathology of geographic atrophy—RPE cell death and lesion expansion—via a well-supported axis (RPE oxidative burden, iron accumulation, GPX4/SLC7A11 failure, lipid peroxide-driven ferroptosis), and it coherently addresses both initiating and executing defects. C05 chain is plausible but weaker: it ends at lipofuscin accumulation, which is a risk correlate rather than the executor of RPE loss, and A2E/bisretinoids are largely resistant to cathepsin-mediated degradation, creating an internal tension in claiming lysosomal enzyme upregulation clears them.

t2_reversal_scored.s1: C04 anchors its upstream ligand (DICER1 loss, cytosolic Alu RNA/cDNA) to data actually documented in human atrophic AMD RPE and to RPE degeneration models, giving it a disease-specific causal chain, whereas C08 oxidized-mtDNA trigger is a plausible but generic aging/innate-immunity narrative less uniquely tied to GA pathogenesis, though C08 downstream senescence/SASP/STAT1 detail is strong.
t2_reversal_scored.s2: C08 articulates a deeper, more complete causal chain (cGAS-STING-TBK1/IRF3-IFNB1-STAT1 senescence lock, SASP-mediated paracrine damage, monolayer breakdown), explains chronicity via a continuous self-ligand source, and includes an immunological decoupling rationale; C04 is well anchored in human DICER1/Alu data but its mechanism largely restates that published axis.

t2_reversal_scored.s1: C02 rests on the strongest causal architecture in GA biology — convergent human genetics at the CFH/CFB regulatory node plus clinical proof-of-concept that C3/C5 blockade slows lesion enlargement — whereas C08 cGAS-STING-senescence axis is mechanistically coherent and literature-supported but lacks comparable human validation of causality in GA progression.
t2_reversal_scored.s2: C02 is anchored by the strongest causal evidence in AMD (CFH/CFB risk genetics, complement deposition in drusen, clinical efficacy of C3/C5 inhibitors), but its mechanism is essentially the established textbook pathway, whereas C08 provides a deeper cell-autonomous chain plausibly connecting well-documented RPE photo-oxidative/mitochondrial stress to senescence, SASP, and dropout, with less direct human validation; net a tie.

t2_reversal_scored.s1: C06 offers a deeper, more tightly coupled causal chain to GA lesion expansion — RPE's unique PUFA-rich outer-segment phagocytic load, SLC7A11/GPX4 failure, and ferroptotic death are well-supported, and the KEAP1-NRF2 node coherently addresses both the initiating (cystine import) and executing (GPX4) defects; C09 iron-efflux mechanism is plausible and genetically anchored (HFE, documented RPE iron), but the complement-to-HAMP link and DNA-damage-mediated atrophic death are more speculative and its own logic (iron is upstream of lipid peroxidation) undercuts the claimed exclusivity of a Fenton-DNA arm.
t2_reversal_scored.s2: C09 wins narrowly because it anchors a specific causal chain (HFE-linked hepcidin/ferroportin dysregulation, histologically documented RPE iron accumulation, Fenton-mediated DNA damage driving senescence) in genetic risk modifiers, whereas C06 offers a coherent but largely correlative oxidative-stress-to-ferroptosis narrative that is disease-plausible yet generic; C09 discriminating prediction (uncoupling labile iron from DNA damage without lipid-marker changes) is also a sharper mechanistic test, though C09 HFE-hepcidin directionality is somewhat muddled relative to classical hemochromatosis biology.

t2_reversal_scored.s1: C07 rests on a fully established causal chain—DICER1 loss in human GA tissue, sufficiency of subretinal Alu RNA to kill RPE, and necessity of DICER1 in conditional mouse models—plus supporting human TLR3 variant data, whereas C03 NLRP3-CASP1-GSDMD axis is plausible and spatially well argued but the dominance of pyroptosis as the executor of RPE death in GA remains less directly demonstrated.
t2_reversal_scored.s2: C07 presents a more rigorously validated causal cascade with direct human pathological evidence (DICER1 loss in GA RPE), demonstrated sufficiency via Alu RNA injection, and a well-mapped TLR3-CASP8-CASP3 downstream axis. C03 pyroptosis mechanism is plausible and grounded in established inflammasome biology, but the direct evidence for GSDMD-dependent lytic death as a primary driver of lesion expansion in GA (versus general retinal aging inflammation) is less causally established.

t2_reversal_scored.s1: C02 rests on the deepest validated causal architecture in GA—CFH/CFB/C2/C3 risk variants converge on alternative-pathway convertase dysregulation, and C3b/MAC deposition on Bruch's membrane-RPE is histologically and now clinically corroborated by approved C3/C5 inhibitors—whereas C09 iron/hepcidin axis is histologically real and genetically hinted (HFE modifiers) but remains more speculative as a lesion-enlargement driver, with iron accumulation potentially secondary to RPE death and the complement-to-HAMP link conjectural.
t2_reversal_scored.s2: C02 is anchored in the strongest causal evidence in geographic atrophy—CFH/CFB risk genetics, complement deposition on Bruch's membrane, and clinical slowing of lesion growth by complement inhibitors—whereas C09 hepcidin-ferroportin/Fenton-DNA cascade is mechanistically detailed and plausible but rests on less consistent human data (modest HFE associations) and an unresolved driver-versus-epiphenomenon question.

t2_reversal_scored.s1: C01 offers a multi-scale mechanism linking a specific extracellular enzymatic lesion (6-O-desulfation of perlecan HS) to loss of endogenous CFH regulation at the RPE-choroid interface, anchored to the strongest GA genetics (CFH Y402H affects HS/GAG binding on Bruch's membrane) and hallmark C3d/C5b-9 deposition; its weakness is that SULF2 as the age-related desulfatase in Bruch's membrane is an untested inference. C07 recapitulates a real, causally supported axis (DICER1 loss/Alu RNA accumulation in human GA), but adds little new mechanistic depth and presents a TLR3-CASP8-CASP3 wiring that is contested in the primary literature, where Alu RNA-induced RPE degeneration has been reported to be largely TLR3-independent.
t2_reversal_scored.s2: C07 rests on a causally validated, human-correlated DICER1/Alu RNA axis, but its TLR3-CASP8-CASP3 framing oversimplifies the documented NLRP3/cGAS inflammasome arms downstream of Alu RNA; C01 coherently links the strongest GA genetic risk factor (CFH, whose Y402H variant alters GAG binding) to age-related desulfation of Bruch's membrane perlecan, though SULF2 causality is currently correlative rather than demonstrated—overall a tie.

t2_reversal_scored.s1: C01 constructs a tightly linked causal chain—SULF2-mediated 6-O-desulfation of perlecan HS in Bruch's membrane, loss of CFH docking, and local alternative-pathway dysregulation—that directly unifies the strongest GA genetic risk factor (CFH, including the Y402H GAG-binding defect) with the well-documented C3d/C5b-9 deposition on RPE/choriocapillaris and the known age-related HS desulfation of Bruch's membrane; C08 mtDNA-cGAS-STING-IFNB1-senescence cascade is internally coherent and plausible, but the centrality of type I interferon signaling as a proximal driver of GA lesions is less firmly anchored in disease evidence than complement dysregulation.
t2_reversal_scored.s2: C01 engages the most disease-validated axis in GA (alternative-pathway dysregulation, CFH risk genetics, C5b-9 deposition) and supplies a concrete mechanistic link between Bruch's membrane aging (SULF2-mediated HS desulfation) and loss of local complement control, which explains why regulation fails specifically at the RPE-choroid interface; C08 mtDNA-cGAS-STING-IFNB1-senescence loop is coherent and ties oxidative stress to SASP, but the claim that type I IFN is the proximal driver of RPE dropout is less firmly anchored to GA-specific histopathology and underweights NF-kB/inflammasome branches of STING.

t2_reversal_scored.s1: C04 is anchored in patient-level data (DICER1 loss and Alu RNA accumulation in GA RPE) with a defined, testable signaling cascade to interferon-driven RPE death, whereas C05 rests on a plausible but less established premise that constitutive MTORC1 activity is a causal driver in GA, and it assumes lysosomal upregulation can clear A2E/bisretinoids that are largely undegradable.
t2_reversal_scored.s2: C04 is anchored to human disease data (DICER1 loss and Alu RNA accumulation documented in atrophic AMD RPE, with sufficiency shown in degeneration models) and targets a defined, druggable nucleic-acid-sensing node, whereas C05 premise of constitutive MTORC1-driven TFEB cytoplasmic sequestration as a driver of GA is plausible systems reasoning but less disease-anchored, and lipofuscin/A2E causality remains debated.

t2_reversal_scored.s1: C05 is anchored in the most firmly established GA biology—bisretinoid/lipofuscin accumulation from lysosomal insufficiency—with a textbook MTORC1-TFEB cascade, whereas C08 cGAS-STING-IFNB1-senescence loop is mechanistically deep and coherent but its causal link to geographic lesion progression remains emerging and partly inferential.
t2_reversal_scored.s2: C08 offers a more complete causal chain (oxidized mtDNA → cGAS-STING → TBK1/IRF3 → IFNB1-STAT1 → senescence/SASP → RPE dropout) that integrates oxidative stress, innate immunity, and cell-autonomous degeneration, whereas C05 premise that lysosomal biogenesis upregulation can clear chemically refractory bisretinoids like A2E is weaker, and the asserted constitutive MTORC1 activity in GA RPE is not independently justified.

t2_reversal_scored.s1: C04 rests on a causally supported chain with human data — DICER1 loss and Alu RNA accumulation are documented in GA RPE and are sufficient to induce degeneration in vivo, and cGAS/STING-driven IFN signaling plausibly links nucleic-acid sensing to RPE senescence and death; C09 iron/hepcidin axis is plausible and histologically grounded, but the leap from HFE risk polymorphisms to local HAMP-SLC40A1 dysregulation as a driver (rather than epiphenomenon) is more speculative.
t2_reversal_scored.s2: C04 builds on directly documented human GA evidence (DICER1 loss, cytosolic Alu RNA/cDNA accumulation) with demonstrated sufficiency to induce RPE degeneration in vivo, and the cGAS-STING-IFNB1 cascade is molecularly coherent including the reverse-transcribed cDNA ligand for MB21D1; C09 is mechanistically layered and chemically precise (HAMP-SLC40A1-Fenton-DNA axis, HFE risk variants, ferritin saturation), but its central causal claim in GA remains more correlative, with internal tension in how HFE polymorphisms map onto local hepcidin upregulation.

t2_reversal_scored.s1: C01 wins because it connects an upstream enzymatic modification (SULF2-mediated HS desulfation) to the strongest validated genetic risk pathway in GA (CFH/Y402H and alternative-pathway dysregulation), providing a precise molecular explanation for age-related loss of local complement control at Bruch's membrane. C09 iron mechanism is coherent and genetically supported by HFE polymorphisms, but the causal link between complement inflammation-driven HAMP upregulation and RPE iron overload is more speculative and less tightly coupled to GA's primary pathology.
t2_reversal_scored.s2: C01 engages the pathway with the strongest causal evidence in GA—alternative-pathway dysregulation with C3/C5b-9 deposition and CFH haploinsufficiency—and mechanistically links the CFH Y402H/GAG-binding biology to a specific, testable aging event (SULF2-mediated 6-O-desulfation of perlecan HS in Bruch's membrane). C09 is coherent and grounded in documented RPE iron accumulation and HFE risk modification, but iron overload in GA may be partly epiphenomenon of cell death, and the HFE-hepcidin direction has known sign ambiguities (HFE loss typically lowers hepcidin).
